Security rollout — B-Snap 2.6.1

Security rollout — B-Snap 2.6.1#

This release addresses CA-19, CA-20, CA-27, and CA-28. Apply these changes to the intended development/staging/deployment environment; never copy test credentials. The source change does not edit the deployment’s .env or contact GoWA/cameras.

Database migration#

Run the normal migration command before starting the updated web/scheduler workers:

.\start-local.ps1 migrate

docker compose run --rm migrate

Revision 20261102_high_security follows 20261012_email_retry_expiry. It adds auth_rate_limits and a nullable, unique group_id to health_check_status. Existing global tracker ID 1 and historical data remain intact. Scoped trackers use negative IDs, have a group FK, and are removed with that group. The downgrade removes scoped progress/counters and preserves the original global tracker.

Incoming GoWA webhook authentication#

Generate a private random key using an operator-controlled terminal, for example:

python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(48))"

Store the same generated value in:

Service

Environment variable

B-Snap web workers

GOWA_WEBHOOK_SECRET

GoWA

WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_SECRET, or the applicable device-specific webhook secret

The secret must have at least 32 characters. Do not reuse the B-Snap session key, camera encryption key, or GoWA outbound API credentials. B-Snap never returns or logs the signing secret. Keep TLS verification enabled when GoWA calls HTTPS.

GoWA sends X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256>. B-Snap verifies the exact raw body before JSON parsing, whitelist lookup, logging message content, or running commands. Body size is bounded to 1 MiB. Missing/malformed/wrong/duplicate signatures return 401; a missing/short configured secret returns 503; malformed signed JSON returns 400; an oversized body returns 413. There is no unsigned compatibility mode.

Whitelist, role, camera-group checks, and existing provider-message-ID deduplication remain active after signature verification. A signature authenticates bytes; it is not itself a timestamp or nonce. Existing provider ID retention governs duplicate suppression. Do not rely on signatures alone for indefinite replay protection.

Configure GoWA first, verify its signing configuration, configure the same key on all B-Snap web workers, then restart/recreate the updated workers. For a rolling key change, coordinate the services; there is no automatic accept-old-key fallback. If a relay reserializes JSON, it must preserve the original bytes/signature or be an explicitly trusted signer; otherwise verification correctly fails.

See the upstream signature protocol.

Production settings and proxy trust#

Set ENVIRONMENT=production and generate a private SECRET_KEY of at least 32 characters. Known development/example keys are rejected. The key is omitted from the security settings’ representation. Invalid settings fail before accepting traffic. Cookie Secure defaults to true in production; explicitly disabling it is rejected. SameSite must be lax, strict, or none; none also requires Secure outside production.

For HTTPS terminated by a trusted reverse proxy:

ENVIRONMENT=production
BEHIND_HTTPS_PROXY=true
COOKIE_SECURE=true
COOKIE_SAMESITE=lax
PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://bsnap.example.com

Also set TRUSTED_PROXY_HOSTS to the actual proxy peer IPs/CIDRs seen by B-Snap. Do not copy an illustrative network blindly. Production rejects *, /0, invalid networks, and a missing explicit proxy list when BEHIND_HTTPS_PROXY=true. Direct HTTPS deployments can leave the proxy list empty. Default development trust is loopback; the legacy TRUSTED_HOSTS fallback is development/testing only and is not a CORS domain allowlist. The reverse proxy must send Host and X-Forwarded-For/ Proto correctly and prevent clients bypassing it. Restrict exposed container ports according to the deployment topology.

PUBLIC_ORIGIN is optional when request Host/scheme already match the browser. Use it if the proxy changes the host/port. It must be an HTTP(S) origin without credentials, a path, or query; production requires HTTPS. Use one canonical origin. Starting with 2.6.2 this same canonical origin also applies to the /ws handshake.

Browser mutations / CSRF#

All unsafe methods are checked before authentication DB work. Browser forms and AJAX need matching Origin, or same-origin Referer, or browser-controlled Sec-Fetch-Site=same-origin evidence. Cross-site and sibling-origin same-site browser requests are rejected. Ambiguous/invalid origins and origin-less unsafe cookie requests fail closed with 403 and CSRF_REJECTED.

Native browser POST forms and same-origin fetch already supply this evidence; no form-token migration or JavaScript token handling is required. An HTTP client using a browser cookie must provide correct origin evidence. For integrations use Bearer API authentication without browser session/Remember Me cookies. Supplying a Bearer header alongside browser cookies does not bypass the check.

The only unsafe public exemption is POST /webhook/gowa, protected by its own HMAC. Auth, setup, MFA and logout are included in browser-origin checks. GET /logout only renders a confirmation; actual logout requires POST. Signed media GET requests retain their existing access rules. Requests are never automatically replayed after a CSRF/authentication error.

Shared login/OTP attempt limits#

Password and OTP stages each allow 30 attempts/IP/minute and 10 attempts/identity per five minutes. OTP login and MFA enrollment share the OTP identity window. Attempts are counted before password/OTP checks, including successful attempts. These constants live in app/utils/auth_rate_limit.py, not duplicate config defaults. Atomic PostgreSQL upserts share counters across workers. 429 responses include Retry-After; counter/database failures return generic 503 without bypassing auth. Expired opaque digest buckets are cleaned during authentication; no passwords, OTP codes, or clear IP/user identifiers are stored in this table. Ensure trusted proxy settings are correct so forwarded IPs cannot bypass IP windows.

Health group boundaries#

Status, uptime, history, counts, group choices, SLA, CSV/Excel/PDF report selection, and single/bulk triggers apply the current user’s group. Cameras use association membership; a stale primary-group scalar cannot grant access. NVRs use their existing group relation. Group NULL preserves global access, including operators.

Bulk progress is isolated per group, independent from scheduler/global progress. Repeated triggers for a running scope return 409; PostgreSQL row locks prevent concurrent starts for that scope. Worker queries recheck membership before network work. Restricted bulk checks do not run global email-log cleanup. Existing recovery resets interrupted scoped trackers along with global progress after a restart.

Existing scheduled-report definitions have no persisted group scope; management of these global definitions now requires group NULL. Restricted users can still download their authorized on-demand reports. No report scheduler is introduced.

Verification and operational limits#

Regression tests use mocked camera/GoWA/SMTP transport, isolated SQLite subsets, and PostgreSQL 17 disposable schemas for migration and concurrent limits/progress. No production schema/configuration is modified by the test run. Test real HTTPS proxy headers, native browser forms, GoWA signatures/retries, operator group changes, and worker restart during deployment acceptance. Docker/image and live external integrations still require the operator’s deployment environment.

Cloudflare Tunnel: WebSocket and toast (2.6.2)#

Versions 2.6.0/2.6.1 check WebSocket Origin against the backend URL, even when PUBLIC_ORIGIN is configured for HTTP. This can reject a valid browser when cloudflared forwards HTTPS to HTTP or overrides Host. In 2.6.2 /ws uses the explicit public origin and normalizes default ports while retaining live session, token revocation, recipient, and group checks. It never trusts X-Forwarded-Host as an origin allowlist. Server logs distinguish origin-policy and session rejection without logging cookies/tokens or notification content.

For a public URL of https://camera.example.com, set on every web worker:

PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://camera.example.com
BEHIND_HTTPS_PROXY=true
COOKIE_SECURE=true
COOKIE_SAMESITE=lax

Replace the example domain with the exact browser origin, without /ws or a path. Set TRUSTED_PROXY_HOSTS to the actual connector peer IP/CIDR seen by B-Snap. For a native connector reaching a native local app this may be loopback; Docker can instead present a connector/container/gateway address. Do not blindly trust all Cloudflare edge ranges or *: the directly connected peer here is cloudflared. Keep the existing private SECRET_KEY unchanged and shared across all web workers.

The tunnel service can remain http://<reachable-b-snap-host>:8080; public HTTPS does not require a second TLS endpoint on an isolated local hop. An optional cloudflared httpHostHeader overrides the backend Host; PUBLIC_ORIGIN handles that rewrite. See Cloudflare origin parameters.

Use the updated application code/image. Changing environment alone on 2.6.1 will not fix the WebSocket origin comparison. For a source-built Compose deployment:

docker compose up -d --build b-snap

If BSNAP_IMAGE is pinned, ensure it names the updated image you built/published; a Git push does not publish an image to the registry. A plain container restart does not reload changed env_file settings; recreate the web containers. Then log in through the public HTTPS URL (direct HTTP cannot use Secure login cookies), reload the page, and inspect /ws: successful handshake is 101 Switching Protocols.

If rejection remains, compare the application log: origin mismatch indicates canonical origin/proxy headers; browser session invalid or unavailable indicates cookies, expired/revoked session, inconsistent worker SECRET_KEY, or DB availability. No request reaching the app indicates tunnel routing/Access/WAF/upgrade issues. Share status/log reason only; do not share cookies, tunnel tokens, or session keys.
